correctness.rationale: The counting proof gives the minimum size and polynomial classification with all quantifiers and finite-field conventions. An explicit algebraic incidence-preserving map proves the exact self-isomorphism. Independently structured exhaustive verification over every selected subset of size up to eight and all legal transitions confirms the component spectra and all 153 pairwise distances; the four representative paths were locally checked. No larger graphs are claimed.

originality.rationale: The new result classifies all optimal locating-dominating codes on a particular classical incidence graph, proves their 4-overlap self-isomorphism algebraically, and finds a sharp universal-for-these-18-states reconfiguration capacity and geodesic property. Accessible cited primary texts give relevant general bounds or ordinary-domination (not locating-domination) reconfiguration, not these statements. Remaining risk of unindexed equivalent accounts is explicitly acknowledged.
residual_risks: Unindexed or inaccessible equivalent computations concerning locating-dominating codes of the Pappus graph may exist.
Search cannot prove a universal negative; independent expert originality verification has not been performed.

value.rationale: The exact reconstruction of a classical incidence graph from the intersection pattern of its optimal locating sensors is a structural theorem, not merely a graph invariant count. The two-spare-sensor threshold solves a natural constrained reconfiguration question while the all-pair Hamming-geodesic result gives an optimal transition benchmark. Prior general lower bounds do not supply these facts.
